scope: Actual Unity material assets and active benchmark renderer bindings for camera-facing danchi construction. This contract supplements material_construction_lookdev.json and facade_optics_contract.json; it does not replace rendered evidence.
target: late-1990s-to-circa-2000 Kanto Japanese new-town fallback, midsummer daylight, built-in Standard shader fallback

physicalMaterialBindings.manufacture: extruded aluminium rail/sash member with anodized oxide finish
physicalMaterialBindings.finish: low-satin silver-gray, fine extrusion direction, no painted edge highlight
physicalMaterialBindings.uvAging: oxide dulling/water spotting only; no directional lighting baked into pigment
physicalMaterialBindings.angularFresnelResponse: subdued metallic reflection frontally, stronger but broadened edge response at grazing angles
physicalMaterialBindings.geometryVsMaterial: extrusion section, joints, plates and fasteners are geometry; extrusion grain/oxidation are material response

physicalMaterialBindings.manufacture: formed/pressed zinc-coated ferrous hardware and fasteners
physicalMaterialBindings.uvAging: zinc oxidation and localized coating breach only
physicalMaterialBindings.angularFresnelResponse: compact metallic response with oxidized broadening; never paint-like or chrome
physicalMaterialBindings.geometryVsMaterial: plate/clamp/bolt dimensions and stand-off gaps are geometry; zinc microtexture/oxidation are material response

physicalMaterialBindings.manufacture: extruded rigid unplasticized PVC drainage/rainwater pipe; mechanically retained by separate galvanized stand-off clamps
physicalMaterialBindings.finish: medium gray high-roughness weathered polymer, non-metallic and non-emissive
physicalMaterialBindings.uvAging: mild chalking/bleaching on exposed face; broad runoff belongs to causal weathering
physicalMaterialBindings.angularFresnelResponse: weak dielectric front response with modest grazing lift; must never read as galvanized metal
physicalMaterialBindings.geometryVsMaterial: pipe diameter, clamp stand-off and wall gap are geometry; polymer grain/chalking are material response

researchBasis.relevance: Documents rigid PVC rain-gutter commercialization in Japan from 1957 and long-term adoption, supporting PVC-U as a period-plausible circa-2000 fallback rather than the previous concrete material assignment.
researchBasis.limitation: Exact pipe manufacturer/model for this fictional benchmark remains unverified; this is period-plausible fallback construction, not a claim about a specific real housing complex.

physicalMaterialBindings.manufacture: RC substrate plus cementitious leveling/render and aged exterior protective coating
physicalMaterialBindings.uvAging: UV chalking and rain exposure are causal layers, not painted light
physicalMaterialBindings.angularFresnelResponse: broad diffuse response with slight dielectric grazing lift only
physicalMaterialBindings.geometryVsMaterial: slab lip/edge break is geometry; coating aggregate/chalking are material response

assemblyBindings.reason: These visible members are aluminium extrusion/sash/rail parts; mixed mid-metallic values create neither believable dielectric coating nor believable metal reflection.
Anchorage and clamp hardware is zinc-coated ferrous metal with metallic reflection broadened by oxidation.
The full-height visible drainage pipe previously inherited a concrete material shared with structural masses. The pipe body is now a distinct PVC-U assembly while clamps remain metal.
The lip is part of the reinforced-concrete balcony slab silhouette and must not inherit the aluminium rail material.

interfacesAndExposure.downpipe: Pipe stands off the facade through galvanized clamps at roughly 1.55 m spacing. Rainwater exposure and UV affect the exterior face; wall-facing recess stays dirtier. Pipe/clamp contact is geometry and contact shadow, not an albedo stripe.
interfacesAndExposure.balconyLip: Lip continues the concrete slab edge and receives rain/sun exposure; drip residue may occur only beneath the physical ledge.
interfacesAndExposure.rail: Manufactured aluminium members repeat regularly; base plates/bolts introduce material and contact-response differences without randomizing construction.
